bibliography.note: The research note forage_fish_early_life.md links the 'thesis abstract' to Deep Blue item 8a87c33f-8b48-4022-a2ea-78541cc47786, which a search result titles 'Parental care sex differences in the brown bullhead…' (the 1986 Behav. Ecol. Sociobiol. paper), not the thesis; the thesis record is item 60e33db4-7a1e-41a3-9f57-1b5fc3ae605a. So the note's 'thesis abstract' may have been read from the 1986b paper's record.

claims.claim: brood attendance raised survival mainly against predation (Blumer 1982, thesis abstract)
claims.note: Neither the thesis nor its abstract could be read. A search-engine summary of the Deep Blue record (secondary; not usable) says adult-removal experiments showed attendance benefits offspring survival and that 'a major function' of care is to minimize predation. Caution for the rewrite: the abstract of Blumer 1986a (see Blumer_1986a) adds that broods failed even when predators were excluded (fungus, gas exchange), so 'mainly against predation' may overstate it; 'a major function is to minimize predation' is the safer wording.
